fatal_errors: The cited evidence concerns synthesis of high-entropy diboride powders, not densification of single-phase ZrB2 bodies at 1800–1900 °C; powder-formation temperature is incorrectly treated as evidence for consolidation temperature.
No cited evidence supports improved strength, reduced porosity, or resistance to prolonged molten-aluminum exposure for the proposed precursor-derived ZrB2.

The proposed transient-liquid mechanism is not established by the evidence, which instead describes organic-to-inorganic conversion, oxide/carbon/boron-oxide intermediates, reduction, and solid-solution formation.

The experiment inconsistently proposes conventionally sintered samples above 2300 °C while also saying both groups receive identical consolidation conditions, preventing a clean attribution of performance to precursor processing.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad temperature, porosity, and liquid-exposure problem and offers a distinct, falsifiable precursor-processing alternative. It does not reconstruct the target intervention: the target uses 30% AlFeNiCoCr binder and SPS near 1500 °C, with liquid-binder pore filling and a 1600 °C binder-loss limit. None of the target composition, SPS schedule, molten-Al conditions, temperature-series baselines, wear test, or optimum-performance mechanism is recovered. The suggested characterization and comparative exposure measurements are generally useful, but the bath chemistry and temperature are unspecified, exposure duration is arbitrary, and processing variables are confounded. Most importantly, the cited high-entropy-powder work does not validate dense single-phase ZrB2 fabrication or service resistance, so the central performance prediction remains unsupported.
